mission: Aevyn turns fully on Ben. His unstable cold white-blue blade becomes the first sustained lightsaber duel of the book. The duel happens across the collapsing Glasswell: rising water, cracking pale mineral, broken survey scaffolds, mirror-lake reflections, unstable holocron cache nearby, Aevyn’s cold white-blue unstable blade fracturing more visibly when his control strains, and Ben’s steadier Jedi blade. The fight is not simply Jedi versus dark sider. It is two students of Jacen arguing through action over what his lessons mean. Aevyn uses a technique that hits something buried in Ben — the corridor moment surfaces as a fragment for Aevyn here, never as exposition. Ben wins by using what Jacen taught him without surrendering ownership of himself. He does not violate Aevyn’s mind and does not pretend Jacen taught him nothing real.
why_now: Chapter 32 occupies the climax phase and carries the next locked outline turn.
conflict: The duel is an argument through action. Avoid thesis dialogue; let blade choices, restraint, refusal, and survival carry the meaning. The blade’s instability tracking Aevyn’s emotional state is a visual tell — when Ben uses Jacen-derived logic successfully, the blade fractures more visibly.
turning_point: Aevyn is defeated as the Glasswell gives way.
closing_hook: Aevyn is defeated as the Glasswell gives way.
setting: Iresh, the Glasswell main chamber — now mostly flooded, the basin a churning sheet of white-blue water. Ben and Aevyn duel across a tilting durasteel survey platform bolted into the mineral shelf. The platform groans and shifts; pale mineral cracks spider across the walls; falling scaffold sections crash into the rising water. Aevyn's white-blue blade casts cold light with no heat in it.
